images.title: Why facing angles are equal
images.purpose: Show that b and d are both 180 minus a, so b equals d, without using any number.
images.composition: Two crossing lines in the centre with angles a, b, d highlighted; two short equations below, the conclusion last.
exact_structure: Two straight lines crossing at one centre point, one horizontal and one leaning; angles labelled clockwise from upper left: a, b, c, d.
Angle a (upper left) is filled reddish purple (#CC79A7).
Angle b (upper right) and angle d (lower left) are both filled teal (#0072B2) and drawn exactly the same size; a and c are the same size.
Angle c (lower right) is drawn with a plain outline, no fill.
Three lines of text below the figure: a + b = 180°, a + d = 180°, then the conclusion b = d in teal.
rejection: b and d drawn with different sizes
any measured angle number on the figure
a, b, d not highlighted as described
images.takeaway: Both b and d are 180 minus a, so they are equal for every a.
images.description: Two crossing lines with angle a in purple, angles b and d in teal, and the equations a + b = 180, a + d = 180 and b = d.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students read the two linear pairs that share a and see that b and d must match.

image_decisions.why: The proof needs a symbolic picture, not measured numbers.
